concerns.text: US-1 scenario 1 requires SI unit conversion ('all units are converted to SI standards') and canonical treatment-type mapping (scenario 2: 'O2 Plasma'/'Oxygen Plasma'/'O2-plasma' → 'Oxygen Plasma'), but no FR covers either behavior. FR-001 covers retrieval/parsing only; FR-002 covers imputation and one-hot encoding. Add an FR for unit normalization and categorical canonicalization, anchored to US-1.

All three Edge Cases state mandatory system behavior ('System must exclude or aggregate', 'System must detect unit mismatches via schema validation', 'System must still report this result as a valid null finding') but none is backed by an FR or SC. Add FRs (or fold into existing FRs) covering sparse-group handling, unit-mismatch detection/conversion, and null-result reporting, each anchored to the relevant story.

US-3 scenario 3 requires bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals on R² in the final report, but FR-007 lists only 'R², RMSE, MAE, p-value, and feature importance rankings' — the CI is missing from the FR list. Amend FR-007 to include the confidence interval (AnalysisResult already has a `confidence_interval` attribute, so the entity supports it).

concerns.location: spec.md:US-1 Scenario 3 vs FR-002 vs Assumptions
concerns.text: Imputation scope is stated three different ways: US-1 Scenario 3 says 'median roughness of the specific substrate class', FR-002 says 'median of the specific feature' (global), and the Assumptions section says 'median-imputed per substrate class per FR-002' — but FR-002 does not say per substrate class. Pick one rule (per-substrate-class median) and align FR-002 and US-1 Scenario 3 to it.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-1 Scenario 1, Key Entities, Edge Cases
concerns.text: Unstable field naming for the same concept: 'plasma_power_watts' (US-1 Scenario 1), 'plasma_power_w' (TreatmentRecord entity), and 'plasma_power' (Edge Cases). Standardize on one canonical name.

concerns.location: spec.md:US-2 Independent Test vs US-2 Scenario 1
concerns.text: Two different runtime thresholds for the same training job: 'completes within 4 hours' (Independent Test) vs 'runtime < 3.5 hours' (Scenario 1). These should be a single consistent bound.

Assumption commits to SHAP via TreeExplainer 'for tree-based models', but the Edge Case explicitly contemplates the best model being Linear Regression, for which no SHAP method is specified. Add the fallback (e.g., LinearExplainer/KernelExplainer) so FR-006 remains satisfiable in that branch.

Edge case requires the system to 'detect unit mismatches via schema validation and apply conversion factors or raise a specific error' for kW-vs-W and min-vs-s. Schema validation alone cannot distinguish kW from W if the column is unlabeled; the detection rule (e.g., value-range heuristic, explicit source-unit metadata, or a documented conversion table per source) is unspecified, so an implementer cannot know when to convert vs raise. Specify the detection mechanism or state that conversion is driven by per-source unit metadata.

Scenario 1 demands real NIST/Zenodo CSVs 'containing mixed units and missing plasma power values'. Whether the actual fetched corpora exhibit exactly these defects is not guaranteed; the test is only reachable if a synthetic fixture is sanctioned. Add that this scenario is verified with a committed synthetic sample file (helper-level fixture), not by requiring the live datasets to contain these specific defects.

'reports a validation R² ≥ 0.0 (indicating no negative performance)' is trivially satisfiable and does not discriminate pass/fail meaningfully. Either state it as a smoke check (job completes, metrics emitted) or tie it to the SC-001 target reporting; as written it is measurable but vacuous.

Under-reach: the idea's methodology sketch requires four visualizations — '(i) predicted vs actual scatter plots, (ii) residual histograms, (iii) SHAP summary plots, and (iv) parameter-response curves'. The spec only covers the SHAP summary plot (US-3 scenario 2). Predicted-vs-actual, residual histograms, and parameter-response curves are dropped with no stated reason; parameter-response curves are the primary deliverable for the 'quantitative relationship' research question.

Under-reach: the idea's statistical reporting requires 'significance of each predictor (p < 0.05) using linear model coefficients where appropriate'. The spec only includes a model-level permutation test (FR-005); per-predictor significance testing is absent, weakening the 'quantify how treatment variables drive adhesion strength' goal.

Under-reach (minor): the idea's feature extraction includes '(vii) polymer-substrate pair identifiers' as an encoded feature. The TreatmentRecord entity and FR-002 (one-hot encode only 'categorical treatment types') omit polymer-substrate pair identifiers as model inputs, though the edge case references polymer-substrate pairs. Clarify whether pair identity is a feature or excluded.

FR-004 mandates a stratified 70/15/15 train/validation/test split based on `treatment_type`. This split can cause data leakage because records sharing the same polymer‑substrate pair (or other correlated identifiers) may appear in both training and test sets, violating the independence assumption required for valid out‑of‑sample evaluation. The methodology should instead group by polymer‑substrate pair (or another appropriate grouping variable) and perform a grouped split, or otherwise ensure that no information about a given experimental system is present in both training and evaluation folds.
